findings.problem: TODO claims 'use Rayon and SmallVec because it will be faster' for a 4-byte input with no benchmark, profiler, baseline, or measured workload to support the claim.
findings.failure_mode: Rayon introduces thread-pool dispatch overhead that vastly exceeds any throughput gain for 4 elements, guaranteeing slower performance on all realistic hardware. The folklore justification ('because it will be faster') violates Holzman performance discipline: 'For tiny fixed-size inputs, avoid parallelism and heap collections unless measured.'
findings.fix: Remove the Rayon TODO. If SmallVec is adopted, justify it only by measured allocation profile showing heap Vec is a hotspot. Name workload, baseline command, baseline number, target hardware, threshold, and variance before any change.

findings.problem: Suggestion to use Rayon on a 4-element fixed-size input directly contradicts the performance defaults: Rayon is 'not a default for tiny fixed-size data' and requires scaling evidence.
findings.failure_mode: Spawning a Rayon work item for 4 bytes will serialize slower than the sequential iterator due to task submission, thread wake, and result aggregation overhead. The fix would regress performance by 1-2 orders of magnitude on any practical input.
findings.fix: Delete the Rayon suggestion entirely. Rayon is appropriate for bulk pure transforms with measured scaling, not fixed-size 4-byte classification.

findings.problem: Vec::new().collect() on line 6 uses unbounded heap allocation with no try_reserve, no capacity guard, and no Allocation error path. For a known-max input of 4 elements, this allocates a heap Vec unnecessarily.
findings.failure_mode: If the function were ever generalized to larger inputs without capacity guards, allocation failure would be unhandled (OOM panic). Even at size 4, heap allocation is avoidable for a known-size output.
findings.fix: Use SmallVec<[&'static str; 4]> from the start, or call Vec::with_capacity(4).try_reserve(4) and map allocation failure to a typed error.

findings.problem: No allocation profiling evidence exists to show that heap Vec allocation is a hotspot or that SmallVec adoption would reduce measurable overhead.
findings.failure_mode: Unmeasured optimization may introduce code complexity (new dependency, type changes) for zero measurable gain. SmallVec is only justified when the small-size distribution is known and measured.
findings.fix: Run a profiler (e.g., samply, flamegraph, or perf) or allocation tracker (e.g., dhat, pretty_bap) to establish whether heap allocation is a hotspot before adopting SmallVec.

findings.problem: No benchmark harness, benchmark binary, or criterion/criterion-like setup exists in the crate to validate any performance claim about classify_four.
findings.failure_mode: Any performance optimization (Rayon removal, SmallVec adoption, loop unrolling) has no measurable baseline to compare against. Without a benchmark, changes are blind.
findings.fix: Add a criterion or basic benchmark binary that measures classify_four with representative inputs across multiple iterations, reporting mean, median, and variance.

findings.problem: No baseline benchmark command or baseline number exists. The TODO performance claim has no reproducible command to run, no baseline measurement, and no variance threshold.
findings.failure_mode: Without a named command, baseline number, and variance, no one can reproduce or verify a claimed improvement. Performance becomes opinion rather than evidence.
findings.fix: Document: (1) the benchmark command, (2) the baseline number in ns/iter, (3) the target hardware, (4) the improvement threshold, and (5) the acceptable variance before declaring success.
